descriptionOfficial.text: The House of Representatives comprises 435 Representatives. The number representing each State is determined by population, but every State is entitled to at least one Representative. Members are elected by the people for 2-year terms, all terms running for the same period. Representatives must be residents of the State from which they are chosen. In addition, a Representative must be at least 25 years of age and must have been a citizen for at least 7 years.

descriptionOfficial.text: The United States Tax Court is a court of record under Article I of the Constitution of the United States (26 U.S.C. 7441). The court was created as the United States Board of Tax Appeals by the Revenue Act of 1924 (43 Stat. 336). The name was changed to the Tax Court of the United States by the Revenue Act of 1942 (56 Stat. 957). The Tax Reform Act of 1969 (83 Stat. 730) established the court under Article I and then changed its name to the United States Tax Court.

descriptionOfficial.text: The United States Court of Federal Claims has jurisdiction over claims seeking money judgments against the United States. A claim must be founded upon the Constitution, an act of Congress, an Executive order, a contract with the United States, or Federal regulations. Judges are appointed by the President for 15-year terms, subject to Senate confirmation. Appeals are to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit.

name: Undistributed offsetting receipts
desc: Not an organisation. The Monthly Treasury Statement nets these receipts against total outlays without assigning them to any agency or branch, so this line sits beside the three branches: Other Interest (-$5.85M); Employer Share, Employee Retirement (-$134.39B); Interest Received by Trust Funds (-$215.94B); Rents and Royalties on the Outer Continental Shelf Lands (-$7.76B); Sale of Major Assets (-$1.44M). Total Outlays is the branches' figures plus this line, to the cent.
